clue.text: Ragout for Henry and company, say

indicators.note: say tells the solver to speak the phrase and listen to how it comes out

parts.note: Henry is familiarly Harry, and company is abbreviated Co., giving a firm called Harry Co.

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a stew suitable for Henry and his friends.
explanation.walkthrough: The stew's name is French, so its final T is silent and it is pronounced like 'Harry Co.', a business run by Henry.
explanation.definitionFit: A haricot is a French-style mutton stew, a kind of ragout.

clue.text: Collection of songs " organized "?

parts.note: organized is read as organ-ized, songs set for the church organ, so a book of church songs

explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a book of hymns, the songs sung in church to organ accompaniment.

clue.text: Students' festivity not entirely worthy of the plant

parts.note: in British universities, rag week is a students' charity carnival

indicators.note: not entirely means the printed word is cut short at its end

explanation.surface: A student party falls short of deserving the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragwort is a yellow-flowered weed common in British fields.

clue.text: He'll drive well over 300 yards for my money

definitions.text: He'll drive well over 300 yards for my money

parts.words: He'll drive well over 300 yards for my money
parts.note: sounds like a golfer's long tee shot, but means someone paid by me to drive a car a long way

explanation.definitionFit: A chauffeur is a paid driver of someone else's car.

clue.text: Describing "tomorrow" in the "recorded time" context

parts.note: Macbeth's speech has to-mor-row repeated until the last syllable of recorded time, a word of three parts

explanation.walkthrough: The allusion is Macbeth's 'Tomorrow, and tomorrow, and tomorrow ... To the last syllable of recorded time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trisyllabic means having three syllables, as to-mor-row has.

clue.text: What's afoot with Tom ? He's made use of.

definitions.meaning: a tomcat's foot is literally the paw of a cat
a dupe exploited by another person to do their dirty work

explanation.definitionFit: From the fable of the monkey using a cat's foot to pull chestnuts from a fire, the phrase names a person used as a tool by someone else.

clue.text: Scapegoat's burden

parts.note: the person blamed for others' faults is said to carry this, in a British idiom

explanation.definitionFit: To carry the can is British slang for taking the blame for others.

clue.text: Stories of filling jury vacancies

definitions.meaning: a legal writ summoning bystanders to make up a jury short of members

explanation.definitionFit: Tales are stories; in law, a tales is a writ to supply extra jurors when the panel falls short.

clue.text: By whom Mimi, for one, was noted

definitions.text: By whom Mimi, for one, was noted

parts.words: By whom Mimi, for one, was noted
parts.note: noted means set to musical notes, so this asks which composer wrote the heroine of La Boheme

explanation.definitionFit: Puccini composed La Boheme, whose heroine is the seamstress Mimi.

clue.text: Debris scattered by crew, a : keg perhaps

indicators.note: scattered means the letters of these words are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: Bits left after a crew tipped over a barrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is a link hinting the keg is only one example of the jumbled words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wreckage is the broken remains left after destruction.

clue.text: Quota of Soviet fighters moving from place to place

parts.note: MiG is the name of the Soviet fighter aircraft designers, so their jets are MiGs
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: An allotment of Soviet jets being shifted from base to base.
explanation.definitionFit: Migration is the movement of people or animals from one region to another.

clue.text: Attraction includes a hundred as pecuniary 'profit

indicators.note: includes means the word for attraction holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a lure is something that attracts or tempts
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A draw that brings in a hundred is seen as money made.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money or financial gain, usually with a hint of greed.

clue.text: A type like Feste retires some way off

indicators.note: something that retires goes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Feste is the jester in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night, a professional fool

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean clown character withdraws to a distance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' turns FOOL into LOOF, placed after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloof means distant or apart, physically or in manner.

clue.text: Standard' CID staff

parts.note: the Criminal Investigation Department is associated with Scotland Yard, London's police headquarters, called the Yard
a staff is a stick

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as an adjective (regular CID staff) but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A yardstick is a standard or measure by which things are judged.

clue.text: About now, from time to time

parts.note: re means about or concerning
currently means now, at present

explanation.surface: A remark on the present moment, every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Recurrently means happening again and again at intervals.

clue.text: English set pace for a change, in obstacle racing

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: An English runner set the pace for once in a hurdles race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges ENGLISH SET PACE; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Steeplechasing is horse or foot racing over fences, ditches and water jumps.

clue.text: "Smooth as monumental ——" (Othello)

parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation: Othello compares sleeping Desdemona's skin to the white stone of tomb effigies

explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a smooth white stone often carved for monuments and tombs.

clue.text: Rover's behaviour may be alarming

parts.note: Rover as a typical pet name, a hound whose barking raises the alarm

explanation.definitionFit: A watchdog is a dog kept to guard property and warn of intruders by barking.

clue.text: Sky-lights for igloo dwellers

parts.note: not windows in a roof but the glowing lights in the Arctic sky seen by people living in snow houses

explanation.definitionFit: The northern lights are a display of coloured light in the far northern sky, where Inuit traditionally built igloos.

clue.text: Church screen of the rose-red 'variety

indicators.note: variety suggests a different form of the same letters, here rearranged

explanation.surface: A church partition in a pinkish shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: Written in metrical form, or the opposite ?

definitions.meaning: composed as poetry rather than prose

explanation.definitionFit: Split in two, the word means composed as poetry; as one word it means the contrary.

clue.text: Greece, we hear, produces such pictures for the screen

definitions.text: Greece, we hear, produces such pictures for the screen

parts.words: Greece, we hear, produces such pictures for the screen
parts.note: Greece sounds like grease, which makes things slip, and also projected photographs

explanation.definitionFit: Slides are transparencies shown on a projection screen, and grease causes skids and slips.

clue.text: Anxiety about contact providing the scroll work

indicators.note: about means the word for anxiety goes round the next piece

parts.note: care means worry or anxiety
touch means contact

explanation.surface: Worry over getting in touch leads to some decorative writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A cartouche is an ornamental scroll-shaped tablet or frame, as in architecture or Egyptian hieroglyphs.

clue.text: It's grand without the spoken dialogue

definitions.text: It's grand without the spoken dialogue

parts.words: It's grand without the spoken dialogue
parts.note: grand describes the sung-through form of musical drama, with no speaking parts

explanation.definitionFit: Grand opera is sung throughout, unlike forms with spoken passages.

clue.text: Iron block in a suburban. villa

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A heavy metal lump found in a house in the suburbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of 'suburban' and the start of 'villa'.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block on which a smith hammers metal.

clue.text: Evade the trick

explanation.definitionFit: To dodge is to evade, and a dodge is a crafty scheme or ruse.

clue.text: Lacking in schooling and badly turned out

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are put together wrongly, in a new order

explanation.definitionFit: Untutored means without formal teaching or instruction.

clue.text: French article about river vessel?

indicators.note: about means the article goes round the next piece

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article

explanation.surface: A French word goes round a river boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: An urn is a vase or container, especially for ashes.

clue.text: Georgia's principal supplier of heat?

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia, so Georgia's is GA'S
main means chief or principal

explanation.surface: Asks who is the leading provider of warmth in a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas main is the large pipe carrying fuel gas that heats homes.

clue.text: Bouncers whose object is to put people out

definitions.text: Bouncers whose object is to put people out

parts.words: Bouncers whose object is to put people out
parts.note: reads as nightclub doormen ejecting customers, but means cricket deliveries meant to get batsmen out

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bouncer is a short ball that rears up; these are another kind of delivery, pitched at the batsman's feet to bowl him out.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkers are cricket balls pitched right at the batter's feet, aimed at hitting the stumps and dismissing them.
